_transcription: PAGE MAP — the booklet is 12 rendered pages (idx 0..11 = printed folios 1..12) and EVERY page is accounted for. idx 0 = bilingual cover (Series A3BAB/1, SET-3, Q.P. Code 55/1/3, 'PHYSICS (Theory)', Time allowed 2 hours, Maximum Marks 35, '12 printed pages'). ENGLISH = the EVEN indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (folios 3, 5, 7, 9, 11). HINDI = the ODD indices 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 (folios 2, 4, 6, 8, 10). idx 11 (folio 12) is BLANK apart from a QR code, an asterisk, the code '.55/1/3', the '256 C' box and the folio number — confirmed AT FULL SIZE, not from the contact sheet, because the brief records a sibling paper whose blank last page carries a mirrored scanner ghost that reads as English at thumbnail size. This one carries no ghost. The alternating hypothesis HELD exactly: the top ~30% of every odd page was cropped and read, and all of idx 3, 5, 7, 9 carry Devanagari from their FIRST line — no English overflow onto an odd top, no English-only final page, and no mid-paper parity inversion. Each English page also ends at a natural block boundary (idx 4 at Q4(b)(ii), idx 6 at Q9(b)(ii), idx 8 at Q12 part I's fourth option, idx 10 at part V plus the end-of-paper rule), so nothing was left to spill. Question numbering runs 1..12 unbroken with every sub-part present. GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS (idx 2) agree with the term2_sci table exactly: 12 questions all compulsory, three sections, A = Q1-3 @2, B = Q4-11 @3, C = Q12 case study @5 (= 35). ⚠ TWO DISAGREEMENTS WITH THE SCIENCE ADDENDUM, both about Chemistry facts generalised to the pattern — see the report. (1) This paper prints SEVEN instructions, not six, and (vi) IS an internal-choice line ('There is no overall choice in the question paper. However, internal choice has been provided in some of the questions.'); the addendum states that term2_sci papers print no such line at all. It gives NO COUNT, so the count was still established by walking the marking scheme. (2) wave.ts reports 'n/a (no MCQs)' for this paper and that is FALSE — Q12 is five keyed 1-mark MCQs, exactly as the dispatch warned. INTERNAL CHOICE: exactly THREE bare 'OR' lines on their own line in the marking scheme (Q1, Q4, Q9), each confirmed against a printed 'OR' on the English page and an 'अथवा' on the facing Hindi page. No other scheme 'OR' exists; the 'Alternatively' markers (Q3, Q5, Q9a) are equivalent answer forms, not choices, and were excluded. Primary-branch marks: 2+2+2 + 3*8 + 5 = 35. DECIMAL POINTS on this artifact are ORDINARY BASELINE FULL STOPS — read off THIS paper at 2.8x magnification (2.014102, 3.016049, 4.002603, 1.008665, 0.30 nm, 0.2 mm, 0.8 mm, 0.4 mm, 1.0 x 10^11) — AND THE PAPER DISAGREES WITH ITS OWN MARKING SCHEME, which prints the same masses with RAISED dots (2·014102) and writes '7·5 mm' in the very line that also writes '7.5'. Following the PAPER, per the brief. SECTION-C KEY: taken verbatim from the marking scheme's own SECTION-C table on ms idx 9, which prints '12. I (B) / II (C) / III (D) / IV (C ) / V(C)', 1 mark each, total 5. Labels there are plain A-D and the paper prints plain (A)-(D), so no positional mapping was needed. All five were ALSO re-derived independently before the table was read, agreeing 5/5 — the key is what ships. VOID: one, on Q10, outside Section A (there is no Section-A MCQ on this pattern) — see that row's _cbseVoided. FIGURES: this paper prints ZERO figures, verified on my own pages idx 4/6/8/10 rather than inherited from the opener. Every 'draw / plot / trace' instruction (Q1a, Q1b, Q3, Q6, Q9b) is the STUDENT's drawing; the marking scheme's diagrams sit inside its ANSWERS. Deliberately no _figure flag on any row. OVERLAP WITH THE OPENER 55/1/1: 15 of 19 rows, matched on CONTENT not position — the sets are reshuffled and no shared row keeps its number. Their stems, options and answers are reused byte-for-byte from data/2022-55-1-1.questions.json AFTER confirming each against my own page, so they dedup at commit.

questions._flag: TYPESETTING DEFECT in the printed stem, normalised rather than reproduced literally — flagged so the choice is visible. The page (idx 4, confirmed at 3x) prints the two refractive indices with their subscripts LOST to the baseline: 'refractive index µ1', 'refractive index µ 2 (> µ1)' — note also the stray space inside 'µ 2'. They are unambiguously \(\mu_1\) and \(\mu_2\): the marking scheme (ms idx 4) sets them as proper subscripts throughout its worked answer, and the stem's own '(> µ1)' comparison is meaningless otherwise. Part (i) (1 mark) is refraction and the wave nature of light — Wave Optics / 'Refraction and Reflection of Plane Waves' would fit it; part (ii) (2 marks: identify the radiation + two uses) is squarely Electromagnetic Waves / 'Electromagnetic Spectrum'. questions.context: The principle of superposition is used to understand the phenomenon of interference of light waves. The principle states that at a particular point, the resultant displacement produced by a number of waves is the vector sum of the displacements produced by each wave. Light waves from two coherent sources produce interference pattern. Thomas Young devised a way to obtain two coherent sources using two identical pinholes (\(S_1\) and \(S_2\)) illuminated by a single monochromatic pinhole source S. Using these sources in his experiment known as Young's double slit experiment, Young studied the interference pattern. The pattern consists of alternate bright and dark fringes. The distance between two successive bright or dark finges depends on the distance between \(S_1\) and \(S_2\), the distance of the screen from the plane of \(S_1S_2\) and the wavelength of light used.
questions.stem:
Consider the following waves :
(i) \(y_1 = a \sin \omega t\)
(ii) \(y_2 = a \sin 2\omega t\)
(iii) \(y_3 = a \sin (2\omega t + \phi)\)
(iv) \(y_4 = a \sin \left(4\omega t + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\)
Which pair of the waves coming from two sources \(S_1\) and \(S_2\) will produce interference ?
questions._flag: THE PRINTED PASSAGE CARRIES A TYPO, transcribed as printed: 'dark finges' (for 'fringes') in the last sentence. The same passage spells 'fringes' correctly one sentence earlier ('alternate bright and dark fringes'), which is what identifies it as a printing slip rather than a reading error; confirmed on my own page at magnification (idx 8). Not corrected — the context is the faithful record and feeds the hash. The identical slip is present on opener 55/1/1, so it is CBSE's typesetting, reprinted across the series, not a set-specific defect. Also note this is an MCQ on a paper wave.ts reports as having none — see the paper-level _transcription note.

questions.stem:
Consider the effect on the angular separation of the fringes in a Young's double slit experiment due to the following operations :
(i) the screen is moved away from the plane of the slits,
(ii) the separation between the two slits is increased till fringes are observed.
Which of the following options is correct ?

options.label: A
options.text: It remains constant in both cases.

options.label: C
options.text: It remains constant in (i) but decreases in (ii).

options.label: D
options.text: It decreases in (i) but remains constant in (ii).
